clue.text: Bliss, say, holding up a pair of scales? Naturally, one breaks up!

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits beneath the first, propping it up

parts.note: D and E are two neighbouring notes in a musical scale
Sir Arthur Bliss was an English composer, Master of the Queen's Music

explanation.surface: A question about a composer and some scales, ending in an exclamation about something breaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bliss' is not happiness but the composer Arthur Bliss. In a down entry 'holding up' puts COMPOSER underneath DE.
explanation.definitionFit: In ecology an organism that breaks down dead matter in nature is called by this name.

clue.text: Come up with a paper that is extraordinary

indicators.note: something extraordinary is out of the usual order, so these letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone produces a remarkable newspaper or essay.
explanation.definitionFit: To come up is to emerge or show up, a synonym.

clue.text: Bird after new moon is one-track

indicators.note: the bird's name is placed following the made-over letters
a new version of the word moon is its letters made over

parts.note: a rail is a wading marsh bird, such as the water rail

explanation.surface: A bird seen after the new moon follows one fixed course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' looks like the subject, but it is the last piece; 'new' is the anagram signal and 'after' orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway system running on a single rail is literally one-track.

clue.text: A paint spread to produce surface-sheen

indicators.note: paint spread around is moved about, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Applying paint to give a glossy finish.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin glossy film that forms on old bronze, wood or leather is a surface sheen.

clue.text: Clement almost stocked following wicked crime

indicators.note: the shortened word comes after the rearranged letters
wicked suggests something twisted, so the letters of crime are rearranged
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a shelf that is stocked is full

explanation.surface: A lenient judge called Clement responds to a wicked crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clement' looks like a man's name but is the adjective. 'wicked' signals the anagram, 'almost' the trimming and 'following' the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement as an adjective means lenient and showing mercy, a synonym.

clue.text: Expected to clutch penny in this trick?

indicators.note: the first word grips the second, holding it inside

parts.note: something expected is due

explanation.surface: Someone expected to be paid a penny for a con.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'truck' is an OCR slip for 'trick': DUE clutches P.
explanation.definitionFit: To dupe someone is to deceive or fool them, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Cry of pain? It's the old disc!

parts.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the definite article
an LP is a long-playing record disc

explanation.surface: Someone yelps at hearing an old record.
explanation.walkthrough: YE is the mock-old spelling of 'the', as in 'Ye Olde Shoppe'.
explanation.definitionFit: A short sharp cry, as from a hurt dog, is exactly this.

clue.text: Price so steep, so argue out a settlement

indicators.note: a settlement arranges things anew, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A buyer disputes a high price and seeks a settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: A price so steep that it shocks is described as scandalous or excessive.

clue.text: Taking many minutes when sectioning Mum, gone crazy

indicators.note: letters that have gone crazy are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: A Caesarean section on a mother takes a long time and causes panic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that takes many minutes is lengthy, using up a lot of time.

clue.text: Lines on style from Don Juan, for example

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another follows it

parts.note: tone is a manner or style
a poem is made of lines of verse

explanation.surface: Lines written about the style of the legendary seducer Don Juan.
explanation.walkthrough: Don Juan here is the orchestral piece by Richard Strauss, not the lover or Byron's verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Strauss's Don Juan is an orchestral work that tells a story, an example of the genre.

clue.text: Makes small amount of progress in Winchester

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the place name

explanation.surface: Someone edges forward slowly in the cathedral city of Winchester.
explanation.walkthrough: Winchester is an English cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch along is to advance by tiny degrees.

clue.text: Practise fighting with soldiers in tough old state

parts.note: to spar is to box for practice
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: Training for combat with troops in a harsh ancient land.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek city-state was famed for its rigorous, austere discipline.

clue.text: Fresh catch of herring at one old penny? That was novel in Victorian times

definitions.text: That was novel in Victorian times

parts.note: a cran is a measure of freshly landed herrings
at a price means for a price
d stood for a penny in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: A fisherman sells his herring catch for a penny in the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: D (Latin denarius) was the old British penny. 'novel' is a noun: Mrs Gaskell's book of 1853.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth Gaskell's book about a small town was published in the Victorian era.

clue.text: Eric, senile, surprisingly showing tendency to recover

indicators.note: a surprising outcome shows the letters in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Elderly Eric bounces back unexpectedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Toughness or the ability to bounce back after setbacks is a synonym.

clue.text: High tars used to bring people round

parts.note: high meat or game smells strongly
tars and salts are both slang for sailors

explanation.surface: Sailors reeking strongly are used to revive those who faint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' means strong-smelling, as with game hung too long.
explanation.definitionFit: A pungent ammonia preparation was sniffed to revive people who fainted.

clue.text: English characteristic in correspondence

parts.note: a quality is a characteristic or attribute

explanation.surface: A national trait shows in how the English write letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Correspondence in the sense of exact match or parity between things is a synonym.

clue.text: Amulet is set to look like the real thing

indicators.note: letters that are set are arranged in a new order

explanation.surface: A jeweller mounts a charm so it seems genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: To simulate is to imitate or feign, appearing genuine.

clue.text: Rustling, we hear, in France?

parts.note: the French have an echoic word for the swish of silk skirts, so a rustling as heard in France

explanation.surface: Someone hears a rustling noise while in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is French imitation of the swishing of a dress, borrowed into English for fussy frills.
explanation.definitionFit: The swishing sound of silk dresses, and by extension showy frills, is this French echoic word.

clue.text: Additional clauses for Synge's main characters?

explanation.surface: Extra clauses about the leading figures in a play by Synge.
explanation.walkthrough: J. M. Synge wrote the Irish one-act play 'Riders to the Sea'.
explanation.definitionFit: Additional clauses tacked on to a document, and the horsemen named in the title of Synge's play.

clue.text: Caddis, later on—?

parts.note: the caddis grub develops into a winged insect, and later in spring comes another winged insect named after a month

explanation.surface: A question about what a caddis larva becomes later.
explanation.walkthrough: Anglers use the caddis and a short-lived spring insect named after a month as flies.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-lived winged insect that hatches in late spring, like the caddis-fly a favourite of anglers.

clue.text: Unknown numbers, around the orient, in a ferment

indicators.note: the two unknowns go around the compass point

parts.note: y is an unknown quantity in algebra; two of them give two letters
the orient is the east

explanation.surface: Mathematicians around the Far East are excited.
explanation.walkthrough: Algebra calls unknowns x, y and z; two Ys surround EAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Something frothing like rising dough is bubbling with agitation.

clue.text: Nightbird in garden got out

indicators.note: the bird is placed inside the flower bed

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot
the owl is the classic nocturnal bird

explanation.surface: An owl in a flower bed went away.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman is bowled out when the ball hits the stumps.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a batsman dismissed by the ball hitting the wicket is said to be this.

clue.text: A pitcher holding reeds

parts.note: read as the instrument that gives the note A for tuning, and is played with reeds, not a jug full of rushes

explanation.surface: A jug filled with rushes.
explanation.walkthrough: The orchestra tunes to the A given by this instrument, so it pitches A; it has a double reed.
explanation.definitionFit: The orchestral woodwind sounds the tuning A and uses a double reed.

clue.text: Canute was so unlucky, making tide fall

indicators.note: making the two words into something else signals their letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: King Canute failed to make the tide go out.
explanation.walkthrough: King Canute legendarily ordered the tide back and failed.
explanation.definitionFit: Doomed or unlucky, a synonym; Canute was destined to fail.

clue.text: Frank ahead —— just!

parts.note: going forth means going ahead
just means fair or right

explanation.surface: Someone frank ahead of judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank means direct and outspoken, a synonym.

clue.text: Temporarily fastened, you say, with delicacy?

indicators.note: you say marks a word spoken, giving its sound not its spelling

parts.note: tacked means stitched loosely or pinned for now

explanation.surface: A seamstress pins a garment loosely with care.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicacy in dealing with people is diplomacy or sensitivity.
